exposure: Anti-seizure medications (ASMs) use (polytherapy, monotherapy, no medication)
Specific ASM types (valproic acid, lamotrigine, carbamazepine, levetiracetam)
cohort: Infants born to 759 pregnant women with epilepsy (PWWE) followed up at 21 neurology outpatient clinics across Türkiye between 2014 and 2019.
finding: The risk of congenital malformations (CMs) was significantly higher in infants of pregnant women with epilepsy (PWWE) receiving anti-seizure polytherapy and high-dose ASMs, particularly valproic acid, whereas lamotrigine use was associated with a lower incidence of CMs.
